svg.title: Voltage compensation
svg.desc: Animated. A battery drains from fresh to tired, staying above the dashed compensation voltage, then is swapped for a fresh one. Two rows show the same output. Compensation off: the green volts at the motor shrink as the battery tires, and the shooter's shot lands short of the target. Compensation on: the SPARK scales its output, so the volts at the motor stay the same, a little under the battery's, and every shot lands on target. With it on, the gains mean the same thing on every battery. The compensation voltage is REV's nominal voltage; the battery stays above it.
svg.text: Same output, same volts at the motor, on a fresh battery or a tired one.
With it on, the SPARK always aims for the dashed line's volts, a little under
any battery, so gains tuned with it mean the same thing on every battery.
compensation voltage (REV: nominal voltage): the battery stays above it
